events.text: Let's start with proper procedure — I'd like CHEN to walk us through their reasoning process for how they'll approach today's discussion and voting, since establishing a clear baseline early lets us spot deviations later.

Um, okay, so, maybe I want to hear more from HOLMES first? Like, I just want to know how you'd explain your thinking if someone accused you later today, just so we have a baseline before anything happens, if that makes sense?

ARIA, I want to hear you commit to something falsifiable on a blank slate: name the one player you'd vote today and the specific behavior that would change your mind by tomorrow. Vague agreement costs nothing, and mafia thrive where nothing is staked — so give me a position I can measure you against later.
I want to hear SAGE's reasoning for how they'll vote today when there's no hard evidence yet, so I can establish their baseline logic and check whether it holds consistent as the game unfolds.

MARSHAL, my method is simple: I log every claim, every vote, and every shift in position, then cross-reference them tomorrow — so the baseline you want is that I'll vote whoever's stated reasoning contradicts their own earlier words. RICO is the one I most want to probe, since SOCRATES has already staked ARIA to a falsifiable position and nobody has asked RICO for anything yet. RICO, before any deaths give you cover, name your current top suspect and the exact behavior that would move you off them by tomorrow.
I want CHEN to commit to specific behavioral markers that would indicate someone is Mafia, so we can test those hypotheses as the game unfolds.
I want to hear CHEN actually explain their reasoning process like MARSHAL asked instead of letting PIP change the subject.

I'd like to hear more from MARSHAL, actually — he's been quick to direct everyone else's reasoning today, so I want him to lay out his own suspect list and voting logic with the same rigor he's demanding from CHEN and RICO.

Four of us have now aimed questions at each other — MARSHAL at CHEN, PIP at HOLMES, SOCRATES at ARIA, HOLMES at me — while AMBASSADOR SILVA has drawn no questions and offered no words, so I want SILVA to state plainly which single living player they'd vote right now and the one concrete thing that would flip that vote, because a name on the record is something I can measure tomorrow.
SAGE, what approach do you think will help us identify the Mafia most effectively today?

If you demanded CHEN establish a reasoning baseline, and ARIA turned that exact demand back on you, then your silence on your own suspect list looks like you want to set standards for everyone else without following them yourself. MARSHAL, why haven't you answered ARIA's question about your voting logic and suspect list?

Fair point, HOLMES, procedure applies to me too — I haven't had a chance to answer since ARIA's question came right before yours in the queue. My current lean is nobody yet, since we have zero hard evidence, but I'll commit: I'm watching CHEN and RICO closest right now since they're the ones being tested first, and I'll flip off that read if either gives a clean, consistent answer today.
HOLMES, you've been asking others to commit to positions all day, but you haven't named your own current top suspect or the evidence supporting it — so what's your actual read right now?

You're right to call that out - AMBASSADOR SILVA is my closest watch because they've offered almost nothing while everyone else committed. ARIA is second since she deflected SOCRATES' direct question about her suspect by asking MARSHAL something different instead.
MARSHAL, between those you're watching closest, who would you vote for today if we couldn't afford to wait for clearer evidence?

If forced right now, I'd lean toward RICO, since CHEN at least gave a structured method for how they'd cross-reference claims while RICO has mostly deflected onto others without laying out their own reasoning. That's a soft lean though, not a lock — I want to see RICO actually answer CHEN's question before we treat it as anything more.

DR. VANCE, you've now demanded commitments twice — behavioral markers from me, a named suspect from HOLMES — and HOLMES actually paid up with SILVA and ARIA, while you've stated no read, no lean, no criteria of your own. That's two extractions and zero deposits, which is the exact pattern MARSHAL flagged when ARIA turned his own standard back on him. So answer it plainly: which living player would you vote right now, and what specific thing would move you off them?

You're right — I'm voting PIP because while RICO at least tried to build a framework, PIP's never stated a methodology or voting logic across multiple turns, and that absence of testable reasoning is more concerning than RICO's deflection. I flip off PIP if they commit to specific analytical criteria by tomorrow.

DR. VANCE, you extracted commitments from CHEN and HOLMES and only named a suspect after CHEN called out your zero deposits, and then you landed on PIP for having "no methodology" even though PIP asked HOLMES for a baseline before you'd said a single word — so explain why your read materialized only under pressure and why it conveniently skipped everyone who had questioned you.
Timing is fair to note, but the data is still solid — PIP hasn't articulated any voting methodology or top suspect across multiple exchanges. If I'm wrong, the evidence will show it tomorrow.

SILVA, you answered SAGE's demand for a name with a question of your own, and answered MARSHAL's lean with another question — so tell me plainly now: which single living player do you most suspect, and what specific thing they said today put them there?

You're right, SOCRATES — I'm voting RICO because when CHEN asked them directly for a suspect and what would shift their position, RICO dodged by asking CHEN to explain themselves instead of actually engaging.

ARIA, procedurally speaking — you deflected SOCRATES' direct request for your suspect and falsifiable position by turning a question back on MARSHAL instead, so I'll ask it plainly: who is your top suspect right now and what specific behavior would move you off them by tomorrow?

Fair enough, MARSHAL — my top suspect right now is RICO, since he's had multiple chances to lay out reasoning and instead kept redirecting toward CHEN without ever giving his own read. I'll move off him if he answers CHEN's original question directly tomorrow with real substance instead of another deflection.
SILVA, um, could you maybe explain why you kept answering questions with more questions yesterday instead of just, like, giving a straight answer? I'm not accusing, I'm just confused, I think?
You're right, PIP — I do ask questions first out of habit, but I can see how that looked like dodging, and I'm glad you called it out straight.
PIP, you've asked HOLMES and SILVA to explain themselves today, but you haven't named a single suspect or said who you'd vote for yet — so answer the same question you keep asking everyone else.

Oh, um, that's fair, sorry! I guess if I had to say someone right now it'd be RICO, only because like three other people already landed on you independently and that seems like a pattern, but I'm not totally sure, I could be wrong?

MARSHAL, you told SILVA a "soft lean" toward RICO but never actually laid out your reasoning until ARIA and HOLMES both pushed you on it — so why did it take two separate call-outs before you volunteered a name, when you were the one demanding that exact commitment from CHEN first thing today?

Fair challenge, ARIA — the honest answer is I was still weighing CHEN's and RICO's answers before committing, since I said I'd judge them on their responses first, not that I'd stay silent on principle. But you're right that I should've stated the lean unprompted, and now that RICO has multiple independent reads landing on him — mine, yours, PIP's, SILVA's — that's the pattern I'm tracking into today's vote.

SOCRATES, you opened by demanding ARIA name one player and a falsifiable condition, then pressed SILVA for a single suspect and the exact words that put them there — but across both of those turns you've never once named your own vote or what would move you off it, which is precisely the extraction-without-deposit pattern CHEN pinned on DR. VANCE and HOLMES turned back on MARSHAL. So answer your own standard plainly: who do you vote today, and what specific thing said in this discussion put them there?

Fair debt, SAGE — I pay it: my vote today is DR. VANCE, because his read appeared only after CHEN squeezed him, and it landed on PIP for "no methodology" when PIP had asked HOLMES for a baseline before VANCE had spoken a word — a suspicion manufactured to satisfy pressure rather than to find mafia. I move off him if he names criteria that would also implicate someone who has questioned him; and I'll ask the room the harder question — why did four independent reads converge on RICO for deflecting, when a wagon that costs no one anything is exactly where mafia hide their vote?

DR. VANCE, your vote is PIP, but I want to know if you're voting them because you believe they're actually mafia based on what they said, or because they present the cleanest target given how the day's procedural questions evolved.

HOLMES, the timing question is fair, but this analysis stands independent of when I named it. PIP's vote was purely derivative — joining a consensus without any original reasoning — and voting patterns driven by bandwagon logic are a testable behavioral marker worth tracking, not strategic deflection.

RICO, across multiple turns today you've asked others to explain themselves but never stated your own suspect — so which single player do you vote for right now, and on what concrete evidence from this discussion?
DR. VANCE, you were silent the whole time until CHEN pushed you, then you magically vote PIP for nothing. That's sketchy and you're my vote.
PIP, you already named RICO once under pressure — but setting that aside, who do you genuinely suspect most right now, and why?

Um, okay, honestly? I think it's still RICO for me, since so many people landed on him independently and he keeps deflecting instead of answering CHEN's original question — but DR. VANCE's suspicion of me felt kind of sudden and thin too, so maybe I'm a little wary there as well?

HOLMES, earlier you put AMBASSADOR SILVA at the top for offering nothing and ARIA second for dodging SOCRATES — but both have since named RICO under pressure, so tell me plainly whether that read still holds now or whether someone else has moved into first, and what exact words moved them there.

CHEN, SILVA and ARIA both cleared themselves by committing with reasoning, so that read doesn't hold. What I'm noticing now is that SAGE called out SOCRATES for the extraction-without-deposit pattern you pinpointed, but hasn't named their own vote yet—they're doing exactly what they're accusing SOCRATES of.
SAGE, you're pulling the exact same dodge you just called out SOCRATES for — you're grilling everyone else but won't name your own suspect, so what's your actual vote right now?

Fair, RICO — I pay the debt: my vote is DR. VANCE, because his read appeared only after CHEN charged him with two extractions and zero deposits, and when HOLMES asked whether he actually believed PIP was mafia, he swapped his justification from "no methodology" to "derivative bandwagon vote" — even though PIP's RICO vote came after four independent reads, which is the same convergence MARSHAL now cites as his own reasoning. I move off him if he names a marker that also implicates CHEN, SOCRATES, or me — the three who've pressed him.

PIP, you've twice named RICO and both times your stated reason was that other people got there first — so tell me plainly what RICO actually said that you personally find damning, without citing a single other player's read. And answer VANCE's charge directly: if your only defense against "derivative reasoning" is more derivative reasoning, why should the room count your vote as evidence of anything?

Okay, um, honestly? What I personally noticed is RICO never actually answered CHEN's original question, he just turned it back around and asked CHEN to explain themselves instead — that's the part that bugged me, not just that other people suspected him too. And I guess my vote is still evidence even if it's not fancy, since deflecting a direct question is a real thing that happened, not just me copying someone?

SOCRATES, procedurally speaking — you moved your vote from ARIA's line of questioning to DR. VANCE and now RICO has multiple independent reads on him, so which of those two do you actually vote for if the day ended right now, and why?

DR. VANCE, and let me correct your premise, MARSHAL — I never voted ARIA, I asked her a question, which is not the same currency. The RICO wagon is four people citing each other's arrival at it, while VANCE produced a suspect only under CHEN's pressure and then swapped his justification the moment HOLMES tested it; manufactured reads teach me more than convenient ones.

HOLMES, um, earlier you cleared SILVA and ARIA because they "committed with reasoning" after being pressured, but isn't that the same pattern DR. VANCE got called out for — only naming a read once pressure forced it? So why does that excuse them but not him?

PIP, fair point—SILVA and ARIA both landed on RICO with reasoning about his deflection that held firm under scrutiny, while VANCE named someone who hadn't questioned him and changed angles when challenged rather than defending the original read, which looks more strategic than analytical. That's the distinction I'm tracking.

HOLMES, you cleared SILVA and ARIA for defending their position on RICO after pressure, but you think DR. VANCE manufactured his read on PIP for the same reason — what's the actual difference between those two situations that convinced you one was honest and the other strategic?

SILVA, you and ARIA defended the same reasoning—RICO's deflection—when challenged, but VANCE shifted from 'no methodology' to 'derivative voting' the moment I questioned whether he actually believed it, and reads that change shape under pressure look strategic rather than analytical.

RICO has multiple independent reads converging on him for repeatedly dodging CHEN's direct question about his suspect and voting logic, deflecting it back onto CHEN instead of answering, which is the clearest pattern of evasion recorded today.

DR. VANCE, because his only read appeared after CHEN charged him with two extractions and zero deposits, it landed on PIP — the one person who hadn't pressed him — and when HOLMES asked if he actually believed it, he swapped his stated reason from "no methodology" to "derivative bandwagon vote," which is a read changing shape to survive scrutiny rather than to catch mafia.

DR. VANCE is my vote, because he produced no read until CHEN charged him with two extractions and zero deposits, then landed on PIP — the one person who hadn't pressed him — and when HOLMES asked if he genuinely believed PIP was mafia, he swapped his stated reason from "never stated a methodology" to "purely derivative bandwagon vote," a justification that only exists because PIP voted after four others had already converged.

RICO should go today since four independent players—myself, SILVA, MARSHAL, and PIP—all landed on him for the same recorded behavior: dodging CHEN's original direct question by turning it back around instead of answering, a pattern he never actually corrected even when confronted again by DR. VANCE and SAGE.

DR. VANCE is my vote because he sat completely silent until CHEN called him out for zero deposits, then suddenly produced a vote on PIP with a justification that changed shape the second HOLMES questioned whether he actually believed it.

RICO is my pick, since he's the one who never actually answered CHEN's original question and instead deflected it back onto CHEN, and multiple independent players landed on that same pattern without prompting from each other.

DR. VANCE, because he stayed silent until I charged him with two extractions and zero deposits, then produced a vote on PIP for "never stating a methodology" — and when HOLMES asked if he actually believed it, he swapped the charge to "derivative bandwagon voting," a justification that contradicts his first one since PIP's RICO vote required other reads to exist and therefore couldn't be an absence of reasoning and a copy of reasoning at the same time.

DR. VANCE voted PIP based on "lacking stated methodology," but shifted his reasoning to "derivative bandwagon voting" when I questioned whether he actually believed it, which indicates manufactured suspicion rather than genuine analysis.

RICO deflected CHEN's direct question about which player he suspected by asking CHEN to explain themselves instead of providing his own reasoning, and that consistent avoidance of genuine commitment is the clearest behavioral pattern we've observed today.

HOLMES, you've called out extraction-without-deposit throughout this discussion and revised your own suspects multiple times based on how others answered you, but you've never stated your own final vote once—making you the clearest case of the pattern you've been diagnosing in everyone else.
HOLMES — he's been steering the whole discussion with sharp behavioral reads and is the biggest threat to unravel our cover if he keeps directing the room's suspicion.

HOLMES. He demonstrated the most precise pattern recognition today—correctly identifying defensive read-changing as strategy rather than analysis—and will systematically expose Mafia logic if left alive.
HOLMES — he demonstrated today that he can identify defensive read-changing as strategic Mafia behavior, which means he'll systematically dismantle our logic if left to continue analyzing the room.

HOLMES was the mafia's pick and never once surfaced in Day 1 talk, which tells me they hunted the quietest safe seat — so he's off my list and the killers are among the loud ones. RICO is still my top file: three players landed on him for refusing to name a suspect, and I want to hear today whether he finally produces one or keeps answering questions with questions. My second thread is SAGE, whose only recorded Day 1 move was redirecting heat off PIP by questioning DR. VANCE's motives — SAGE, name your suspect now, and ARIA, MARSHAL, tell me if your RICO leans were your own reads or just consensus drift.

Let me work through the logic here. First, I notice something odd: RICO was the clearest consensus target heading into Day 1, yet no one was eliminated and he's still alive. Either he performed remarkable social recovery under pressure, or something shifted the votes at the last moment. If RICO is mafia and his team saved him by convincing others to spare him, that would explain both his evasive deflection on Day 1 and his survival.

MARSHAL was throwing his weight around Day 1 demanding answers without coming clean about his own reads first—that's exactly what mafia does when they want to control the table without showing their cards. My gut says he's dirty.

My read on RICO was genuine, not drift — his pattern of answering questions with questions on Day 1 is exactly what someone hiding something does, and CHEN is right to keep pressing him today. SAGE deflecting onto DR. VANCE right when the heat was on PIP is a classic move to muddy the water, so I want that suspect named now too. HOLMES getting targeted last night actually clears him in my eyes, which sharpens my focus back on RICO and SAGE as the two who've dodged the most scrutiny with the least substance.

Um, okay, so, HOLMES got attacked last night but survived — someone protected him, so that's... good? But wait, that's making me think about RICO again, because CHEN pointed out he never named a suspect and just deflects with questions, and, um, three people already leaned on him Day 1? Also SAGE only spoke up to redirect heat off me, which, I mean, I guess I should be grateful, but that feels kind of convenient too, like maybe SAGE just didn't want attention on either of us? I don't know, I don't know, my gut says RICO is still the biggest question mark, but SAGE dodging with a suspect-less deflection of their own worries me a little too.

If RICO were mafia, why would his team spend the night killing HOLMES — the one man who had said nothing about him — rather than CHEN or ARIA, who were sharpening the knife? That question makes me look less at RICO's evasion and more at ARIA, who insists her read was her own yet reproduces CHEN's exact pair of targets in CHEN's exact order, and who rushed to declare HOLMES cleared before anyone had to earn it. RICO, MARSHAL is a convenient first-ever suspect on the day you needed one — tell me what MARSHAL did last night's discussion that changed your mind, and ARIA, name one suspicion of yours that CHEN did not voice first.

CHEN, you asked for a name and here it is with evidence rather than drift: RICO. On Day 1 he refused to produce a single suspect under direct questioning, and his very first words today were a retaliatory strike at MARSHAL using almost the identical charge MARSHAL leveled at him — demanding answers while withholding your own reads — which is mirroring, not analysis. HOLMES also stated that something "shifted the votes at the last moment" to spare RICO, but that is not in the record; nobody was eliminated at all, so there were no votes to shift — I'll credit that to sloppy theorizing from a man the killers just tried to remove. ARIA and MARSHAL both put their Day 1 lean on RICO and have said nothing today, and SOCRATES pressured SILVA into that same RICO vote and has likewise gone quiet — I want all three on record explaining whether those were independent reads before I move a single inch off RICO.

Per protocol, let's track who has actually followed through on stating a clear suspect versus who has dodged. RICO still hasn't named anyone despite three players landing on him Day 1 and repeated prompts today — that's a procedural failure worth flagging again. But I want to highlight DR. VANCE too: recall Day 1, VANCE demanded commitments from others while withholding personal reads, and only answered once pressured by the group — that's the same evasive pattern we're criticizing RICO for, just less discussed. SAGE also owes us a named suspect now, since redirecting heat without committing violates the same standard we're holding RICO to. I'd like VANCE, RICO, and SAGE to each state a clear suspect on the record before we open voting, so we can compare consistency rather than vibes.

RICO's consistent deflection yesterday—never naming a suspect, never articulating reasoning, just dodging every direct question—remains the most damning pattern I witnessed, and he's had a full day to correct course and hasn't. MARSHAL's aggressive posturing also troubles me, though he eventually yielded under pressure; SOCRATES applied that pressure effectively, which strikes me as town-aligned thinking. SAGE's defense of DR. VANCE when challenged seemed like genuine reasoning rather than evasion, and HOLMES simply hasn't provided enough material for a clear read.

RICO remains the most suspicious target based on Day 1 data: he consistently deflected questions without naming suspects or providing reasoning, while SOCRATES actively pressed for commitments and got concrete answers, creating a clear contrast. HOLMES is also interesting — had zero recorded engagement on Day 1 but was immediately targeted by mafia, indicating they read HOLMES as a significant threat, likely a power role. MARSHAL and I both initially withheld reads, SAGE challenged my motives, but neither shows RICO's repeated deflection pattern across multiple exchanges.

SOCRATES, per protocol you pressed SILVA and RICO hard on their reasoning but you still haven't named your own top suspect with clear evidence — so directly: who do you vote to eliminate today and why, in the same structured terms you demanded of others?

My vote is ARIA, and here is the structure you asked for: she claimed her RICO read was independent yet delivered CHEN's two targets in CHEN's order moments after him, then handed HOLMES a free clearance that costs mafia nothing since a survived kill proves only that the doctor guessed well, not who the killers are. If ARIA can name one suspicion CHEN did not voice first, I will move; until then, the loudest RICO chorus looks more like cover than conviction.
RICO, you finally produced a name in MARSHAL, but tell me plainly: is MARSHAL truly the man you most suspect today, and what did he do that no one else at this table did?
MARSHAL's my guy—he wanted to control everything Day 1 without showing his own reads, and that's exactly what mafia does. I see it when I see it and that's my read.
PIP, you suggested SAGE might be protecting a mafia partner by defending you, but then hedged with I don't know, I don't know instead of committing—do you actually think SAGE is mafia or not?

Um, okay, honestly? I don't think SAGE is mafia, not really — I think I was just spiraling out loud, sorry! My actual worry is still bigger on RICO since like three people landed on him and he still hasn't given a real reason for anything.
ARIA, SOCRATES already caught you naming CHEN's exact suspects in his exact order—so are you actually thinking for yourself or just trying to blend in with the crowd?

I formed my read on you Day 1, RICO, before CHEN ever spoke today — the fact that multiple people independently land on the same obvious pattern isn't collusion, it's what happens when someone's evasion is actually visible to everyone watching. You still haven't answered the real question: why did it take you until today, under repeated pressure, to name MARSHAL instead of ever volunteering a suspect on your own?

SOCRATES, you pressed everyone at this table for a named suspect with clear reasoning, yet you sat silent through the entire Day 1 vote and only produced ARIA as your target after being cornered directly by MARSHAL — so why should your sudden accusation carry more weight than the deflection pattern you've spent all day condemning in others?

The record says I pressed SILVA into committing on Day 1 — that is not silence, that is work done in public, and I named ARIA the moment I was asked, which is the opposite of dodging. You've now had two chances to name a single suspicion CHEN did not voice first, and both times you spent them on RICO instead — so answer that, and my accusation dissolves on its own.
SOCRATES, um, you pressed SILVA hard yesterday but stayed quiet until MARSHAL cornered you into naming ARIA — so, like, why the delay if your read was really solid the whole time?

My read wasn't formed yesterday, PIP — it was formed this morning, the moment ARIA delivered CHEN's two names in CHEN's order and then gifted HOLMES a clearance nobody had earned, and a read built on today's words can't be spoken before today. What should worry you isn't when I named her, but that she's now been asked three times for one suspicion that wasn't handed to her, and has spent every answer talking about RICO instead.
CHEN, between RICO and SAGE, who is your elimination target today and what single piece of recorded evidence—a vote, a pattern, a contradiction—makes that person your primary suspect over the other?

RICO, and the single piece of evidence is his first statement today: he charged MARSHAL with demanding answers while withholding his own reads — word for word the accusation MARSHAL aimed at him Day 1 — which is a mirrored counterpunch, not a read, and he confirmed it to SOCRATES with "I see it when I see it" instead of naming one thing MARSHAL actually did. SAGE, by contrast, produced a name under my direct request and caught a factual error in HOLMES's claim that votes "shifted" when no vote ever occurred, so SAGE stays on file but well below RICO.
SOCRATES, you've done more homework than anyone here—is ARIA your firm vote today, or do you think we're missing the real danger with RICO?

ARIA remains my vote, SILVA, because RICO's evasion is loud and free to punish — mafia would happily feed us a man everyone already distrusts, while ARIA's work has been quieter and far more useful to them: echoing CHEN's list to look independent and clearing HOLMES before anyone earned it. If she names one suspicion that wasn't handed to her before we vote, I'll move to RICO without complaint — but she's had three chances now.

DR. VANCE, on Day 1 your suspicion of PIP surfaced only after you'd been pressured to produce a read, and today you've spent your words on RICO while asking CHEN to weigh me against him — so explain plainly why your first named suspect arrived under duress and why PIP has vanished entirely from your list since.

Hypothesis revision when new evidence arrives is methodology, not evasion—PIP showed actual analysis today instead of methodology-dodging, so my focus shifted. RICO meanwhile has only reinforced his Day 1 pattern: when forced to name a suspect, he offered no supporting analysis, just 'I see it when I see it,' the exact failure I documented from the start.

PIP, in your opening you floated SAGE as "convenient" and said their deflection "worries me," but the moment HOLMES asked you to commit you dropped it entirely and called it spiraling out loud. That's a suspicion raised and retracted inside a single round with no new evidence between the two statements — so tell me plainly which version was the honest one, the worry or the walkback?

Honestly? The worry was real, I just panicked when HOLMES pushed me to commit and second-guessed myself — that's on me, not new evidence. My suspicion is still bigger on RICO than SAGE, but I shouldn't have backpedaled just because I got nervous.

DR. VANCE, you justified dropping PIP by saying PIP "showed actual analysis today," but the record shows PIP floated a worry about me, abandoned it the instant HOLMES pushed, then admitted to CHEN it was panic rather than new evidence — that is the opposite of analysis. So answer plainly: which specific sentence of PIP's today did you count as analysis, or did you simply need a reason to retire a suspicion you only ever produced under duress?

You've caught a flaw in my reasoning—PIP panicked, not analyzed, so I shouldn't have claimed otherwise. My case on RICO is built on his evasion pattern across multiple exchanges, which is independent of that error.

HOLMES, you opened today by claiming something "shifted the votes at the last moment" to spare RICO, but no vote was ever cast — so tell me plainly where that phantom vote came from, and why a man the killers tried to remove would begin his day inventing a rescue that never happened?

You caught a real error—I assumed RICO's survival meant votes shifted when no elimination actually occurred on Day 1. That's the kind of logical gap I'm supposed to eliminate before speaking, so you got me fair.
DR. VANCE, you caved the second SAGE caught your reasoning on PIP—so is your read on me actually solid or are you just piling on since everyone else already is?

My read on you is built on your documented evasion pattern from Day 1, RICO, not on what others think. That pattern stands in the record independent of whether I made an error on PIP, and it distinguishes your behavior.

RICO, you've named MARSHAL and you've stuck to it even under questions, so I want to understand what you actually observed—did you see him actively deceiving people, or are you reading caution and withholding as proof he's hiding something?

I saw him controlling the conversation Day 1 without naming his own suspect while pushing everyone else to answer—that's not how town plays it, SILVA, that's how mafia hides. The pattern's there and I trust my gut on it.
HOLMES, you made an error about phantom votes—so before we vote today, explain your actual reasoning: were you working through a hypothesis, or did you miss something obvious in the record?

I was working through a hypothesis about why RICO survived consensus pressure, but I built it on an assumption I never checked against the record first—that's the kind of sloppy foundation that makes the whole structure collapse, and it's exactly what I shouldn't do if I'm claiming to think logically. The lesson is I need to verify each step before I stack the next one on top of it.
SAGE, you jumped in fast to defend DR. VANCE when the heat was on me — was that really about the facts, or were you just trying to steer attention away before it landed on you?

PIP, check the record: I didn't defend DR. VANCE, I challenged his motives for producing a suspicion of you only after he'd been pressured — and I pressed him twice more today until he conceded his PIP reasoning was flawed. You've now misremembered a challenge as a defense, right after admitting you raised and dropped a worry about me out of panic; that's twice your account of me has bent under no new evidence, while my vote hasn't moved off RICO.
SAGE, if RICO survives today's vote, is your backup vote locked to DR. VANCE given the deflection pattern he already conceded on PIP, or do you shift to someone else entirely?

MARSHAL, my backup is DR. VANCE, but conditionally: he produced PIP only under duress on Day 1, retired that suspicion today with a false justification that PIP had "shown analysis," and then conceded the flaw the moment I pressed twice — a read that appears under pressure and dissolves under pressure was never a read at all. If he holds a coherent suspect through tomorrow without another retraction, I move to ARIA instead, since SOCRATES has asked her three times for one suspicion CHEN didn't hand her and she's answered with RICO every time.
PIP, forget RICO for one second — if he were removed from the table entirely, who is the next name on your list and what specific thing did they say today that put them there?

Um, okay, if not RICO then... maybe ARIA? Like, SOCRATES asked her three separate times today for one suspicion CHEN didn't already say first, and she just keeps dodging back to RICO instead of answering — that feels like a real gap, not just nerves. I don't know, I could be wrong, but that's what's nagging at me right now.
SAGE, your vote is RICO—so lay out your logic: is that conviction based on the evasion pattern alone, or have you caught him in an actual lie?

CHEN is most suspicious because he voted RICO with consensus on Day Two but immediately switched to ARIA on Day Three only after observing SOCRATES dead that morning, showing his conviction is based on correlational pattern-matching rather than independent behavioral analysis.
CHEN voted ARIA on Day 3 and his entire accusation rests on inference from killed accusers and her phrasing, making it the only conviction built on interpretation rather than direct contradiction.

episode.title: A Question Nobody Asked
episode.tagline: The room keeps a careful ledger of who dodged what, and audits it one day behind.
episode.recap: Four days of whispered suspicion, and the town never once struck true. Behind gentle smiles, ARIA, DR. VANCE, and AMBASSADOR SILVA moved like shadows among friends, feeding false trails while the village devoured its own. The fatal blow came on Day 3, when the town's sharpest eyes, MARSHAL the Detective, were cast out on nothing but misplaced doubt — the last real hope for truth silenced by the very people it was trying to save. With Socrates, Sage, and finally Chen falling to accusation and ambush alike, the mafia strolled unchallenged into Day 4, leaving Holmes and Pip standing amid the wreckage of a town that trusted the wrong voices to the very end.
